evidence.summary: The pinned fingerprint identifies product tuple 0x0129/0x803A/0x0508 and assigns the YRD156 to the base-lock profile used by this record.
On the current handler path, the function derives userIndex, userName, userType, credentialIndex, credentialType, and credentialName records from Z-Wave user-code reports.
The base-lock profile separately exposes lockCodes, lockCredentials, and lockUsers capabilities.
Credential data is accepted as a write-time UserCode payload. The pinned response path records slot occupancy and identity metadata rather than returning or caching the PIN value.
The main driver template registers the current lockUsers, lockCredentials, and user-code report handlers; migrated marker state is emitted only when the persisted migration flag is true.
When SLGA_MIGRATED is unset or false, the pinned can-handle function routes the device to the legacy subdriver.
The explicit legacy migration command emits lockUsers and lockCredentials state and then persists SLGA_MIGRATED as true.
The SDF model defines an array of string lock-code values but no user or credential identity, type, lifecycle, authorization, or privacy metadata.

limitations: No real PIN, lock code, user identifier, or device credential is stored here.
The analysis is based on pinned source artifacts, not device or account tests.
No pinned record establishes the SLGA_MIGRATED state of a real YRD156. Devices without a true migration flag use legacy/default handlers whose user-code behavior is outside this mapping set.
The SDF object is a neutral data model, not an authorization or credential management specification.
Contract version 0.1 lacks a driver-source artifact role; the pinned Lua source is transparently recorded under the generic evidence role.
The conclusion is bounded to the pinned lock-code SDF object; other SDF objects or future extensions might represent identity metadata.
The write path accepts credentialData as a PIN payload, while the report path represents slot occupancy and identity metadata; the files do not establish one reversible value-level representation.
No transformation is proposed for security-sensitive credential values.
